Alex.confusing: How the final bonus was computed: the scores showed large bonuses, such as 39 and 40, that the rules didn't explain, and the "Grudge" doubling on a Meowfia win was never described.

Alex.change: Describe the bonus and doubling mechanics in the rules, and give Farm players more reliable ways to check claims, such as seeing each visitor's egg result.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw 12 and 7 at Finley after one round of talk. Finley's story was messy, but Drew was a cat in the same scenario and the whole table was piling on. I should have thrown low cards, like the wild and the 4, and kept my high ones.

Blair.confusing: How Turkey and hug/confusion interact with egg counts. Players kept contradicting each other about whether a visitor to a Turkey gets an egg. Also unclear was how the final bonus numbers were computed, such as the Grudge doubling.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when the table's reasoning about Finley's hugged-Eagle story clicked and my high stake on Finley banked doubled.
Blair.change: Show each player's role-specific result more clearly, or give Meowfia a stronger way to learn something useful at night. The Sphinx and Floofer gave me almost nothing to work with.

Casey.confusing: How Turkey and Hawk egg counts interact with claims, and how confusion and hugs affect reports. It made it hard to tell lies from true-but-odd results.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when the table converged on Blair and my stake banked 17 points on a correct read.
Casey.change: Show the final standings, or at least each player's stake totals, during play. Then players could balance their own score against their team's.
Casey.regret: In rounds 2 and 3 I staked big cards on a pile-on that turned out to be Farm. I should have thrown small cards and wilds and kept the rest as a floor. In round 3 I also dismissed Finley's hug story, which fit a real Eagle hugged by the Floofer Blair, so I should have weighed it more.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey's direction. In round 1 I first misread it as eggs landing in my own nest, then had to take that back in public. The Meowfia stake rule, which pays 2x only if the Farm player you threw at is the one eggsecuted, also took a while to sink in.
Drew.fun: Round 3 as Meowfia: I claimed the safe Turkey, joined the table's push on Finley, and my 3 high cards banked at 2x. That moved me up to second place.
Drew.change: Make egg counts easier to cross-check. For example, show a per-night log of who gained or lost eggs, or limit how far claims can be bluffed without any verification.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I mixed up the Turkey rule in public and wrongly accused Casey, Blair and Alex. I should have reasoned carefully first: Turkey gives eggs to visitors, so my 0 only meant nobody visited me. I should have kept quiet rather than make false claims. In round 2 I also threw 2 cards on Ellis with only weak evidence.

Ellis.confusing: How the Turkey's egg-laying interacts with visitors' reports, and how banking works with scores (the large bonus numbers in the final tally weren't clear to me).
Ellis.fun: Round 1, steering the table toward Drew as a Mouser while my partner was getting eggsecuted. It was tense, even though it didn't work.
Ellis.change: Show the full scoring formula up front, including how the large bonus is computed, so players can plan around the win condition.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I misread Drew's Hawk claim and my own Turkey reasoning, then flip-flopped and drew suspicion. I should have said calmly that Drew visited me, that I was Farm, and pointed at Alex's Owl claim without contradicting myself. In round 3 I also staked three high cards, 33 points of value, on a consensus vote. I should have thrown fewer.

Finley.confusing: The Meowfia "Grudge" doubling on a banked stake in round 2 wasn't in the rules I read, and the big end-of-game bonus figures weren't explained. I also couldn't tell whether a hugged Eagle still got Turkey eggs.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was the most fun. I was Sphinx and steered the table onto Ellis, a Farm player, and the Meowfia win paid off massively.
Finley.change: Make the scoring bonuses explicit up front, and show the round's Farm animals in play to everyone, so claims are easier to check.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I accused Drew based on a hug theory that ignored how Turkey and Floofer interact. I should have checked the logic before staking big, and I could have argued less loudly. It was still correct about Drew, but it got me eggsecuted.

review.title: Turkeys and Snowballs
review.headline: Finley rode a lucky cat round and a hugged mislynch to a runaway win.
review.summary: Round 1 was a clean Farm win. The table piled on Blair, a Sphinx who bluffed a bad Owl story. In rounds 2 and 3 Farm mislynched its own players. Round 2 hit Ellis, a true Turkey. Round 3 hit Finley, a hugged Eagle. The cats banked big 2x stakes both times. Finley was a cat in round 2 and was the Farm player eggsecuted in round 3, but still banked a stake on Drew. That left Finley far ahead at 115.

rounds.recap: Blair (Sphinx) and Ellis (Mouser) were the cats. Drew misread the Turkey and said nobody visited him, which muddied things. Blair then claimed Owl and said she visited Drew but got no egg. Blair's Owl line also copied Casey's public Tit claim. Everyone threw at Blair, who was eggsecuted, so Farm won.

Alex (Floofer) and Finley (Sphinx) were the cats. Alex's Owl claim didn't fit the egg counts, and Casey and Drew both noticed. But Ellis, the real Turkey, kept contradicting himself, and Drew's Hawk +1 was really Ellis's Turkey egg. The table voted Ellis, a Farm player. Both cats banked 2x stakes, and Finley jumped to 94.

Blair (Floofer) and Drew (Sphinx) were the cats. Drew claimed Turkey, and Finley's +0 after visiting him didn't fit that claim. But Finley also said he was hugged, and the table took the mismatch as proof that Finley was lying. Blair and Alex had both claimed to visit Finley, and Blair was the real Floofer. Nobody followed that up, so Finley was eggsecuted and the cats won.

highlights.text: Blair claimed Owl and said only a Tit visited Drew. Casey saw it was copied from her own public claim, which sank Blair.
Casey's hugged and confused Kookaburra report correctly pointed at a Floofer. The table then voted for Ellis anyway.
Ellis said Drew's visit explained Drew's +1, which was true. The table still voted for him, and the cats banked 2x stakes on a Farm player.
Finley deduced correctly that a Floofer had visited him. He blamed Drew, the Sphinx, instead of Blair or Alex. The consensus then ate him.

confusions.what: As Turkey, he said nobody visited him because he got 0 eggs. A Turkey lays eggs in visitors' nests and gets none itself. He later corrected this himself.
As Turkey, he said his 0 eggs meant nobody visited him, which is the same mistake Drew made in round 1.
Finley argued that a Turkey 'can't know nobody came'. He was right about that, but his argument also cut against the Farm Turkey it was aimed at.
As Hawk, he read +1 as proof that Ellis was Meowfia. Hawk only gets an egg if the target is Meowfia. Ellis's Turkey egg explained the +1 just as well.
As Sphinx, he thought Hawk was not in play and that Turkey was a safe claim. All Farm animals are in the pool, so no animal is 'not in play'.
Alex first said Casey's claim that he visited Finley was wrong, then admitted it fit. Alex was muddled about hug mechanics and who visits whom.
Alex claimed Owl but said he had 'no visitor report', although an Owl learns the animals that visited its target. The claim was sloppy.
Casey said Alex visited Finley as proof Alex was suspicious and asked why a Tit would guess Pigeon. Casey didn't connect two claimed visitors to Finley (Alex and Blair) with the hug.

worked: Egg counts as evidence worked in round 1. Blair's +0 against a Turkey claim, plus her Owl line copied from Casey, gave the table a real, checkable lie to catch.
The Floofer hug plus the Kookaburra confusion in round 2 gave Casey a real clue. It also created a believable false-claim story for the cats.
Cats staking 2x on a mislynched Farm player is a strong payoff for winning a round. It makes round 3 matter and gives the table something to chase.
The three-CAW early end rule let the table settle on a vote quickly once it had a target.
problems: The safe-animal rule does nothing here. The pool holds every animal, so no Farm animal is ever 'not in play'. Cats got no real safe claim, and Drew misread this and thought Hawk was out. Fix: shrink the pool or drop the rule text.

The Turkey is a trap role. Two Farm Turkeys were treated as liars for saying 'nobody visited me', and one was eggsecuted. Fix: give the Turkey a dawn line such as 'N players visited you' so it has something real to claim.
The 2x cat stake snowballs. One cat win with big throws gave Finley 94 and put the game out of reach. Fix: cap the cat bonus, or let Farm banks scale as well.

Table consensus beat evidence. In rounds 2 and 3 players spotted real contradictions (Alex's Owl, the two visitors to Finley) but still voted the loudest target. Fix: reward early-caw reasoning less, or give the Storyteller a reason to prompt follow-up.

Round 1 and 2 night choices were mostly random, so early info was thin. Dawn reports were also hard to compare because of hugs, confusion and unreliable claims. Fix: add a short recap of each player's own dawn report at the start of the day.
